G/SPS/N/CHL/899.title: Establece requisitos fitosanitarios de importación para frutos frescos para consumo de naranja (citrus sinensis) procedentes de Egipto
G/SPS/N/CHL/899.description:
• El proyecto de resolución establece los requisitos fitosanitarios para la importación a Chile de frutos frescos para consumo de naranja ( Citrus sinensis ) de origen y procedencia Egipto.
     
  • La medida establece que los envíos deberán estar amparados por un Certificado Fitosanitario Oficial emitido por la Organización Nacional de Protección Fitosanitaria de Egipto, incluyendo declaraciones adicionales para las plagas cuarentenarias asociadas a la vía.
     
  • Para el manejo del riesgo de Bactrocera zonata y Ceratitis capitata se establece la aplicación de un tratamiento cuarentenario de frío T107-L, a una temperatura de 1,67 °C o inferior durante 18 días, el cual podrá realizarse en origen o en tránsito. Asimismo, se establecen medidas fitosanitarias específicas para Phytophthora palmivora y requisitos de inspección para las restantes plagascuarentenarias reguladas.

 

  • Los envíos deberán proceder de lugares de producción y empacadoras registrados y autorizados por la autoridad fitosanitaria oficial de Egipto, identificados mediante códigos únicos, y deberán cumplir requisitos de trazabilidad que permitan relacionar cada lote con su lugar de producción, empacadora, Certificado Fitosanitario, contenedor y sello o precinto, según corresponda.
     
  • La propuesta contempla además requisitos de muestreo e inspección fitosanitaria, limpieza, lavado y cepillado de los frutos, ausencia de flores, hojas, restos vegetales y suelo, condiciones de embalaje, rotulación, resguardo y transporte, así como inspección fitosanitaria por el Servicio Agrícola y Ganadero al ingreso a Chile.
     
  • Previo al inicio de la primera temporada de exportación, el SAG realizará una verificación técnica en origen destinada a evaluar el cumplimiento de los requisitos establecidos, las condiciones de los lugares de producción y empacadoras, los procedimientos oficiales de certificación fitosanitaria y el programa de vigilancia y monitoreo de Bactrocera zonata y Ceratitis capitata.

 

Para mayor detalle, revisar el documento adjunto a esta notificación.

G/SPS/N/KOR/855.title: Proposed amendments to Standards for Recognition of Temporary Standard and Specifications for Foods
G/SPS/N/KOR/855.description:
The Republic of Korea is proposing to amend the "Standards for Recognition of Temporary Standard and Specifications for Foods".
The regulations on applying for temporary standards and specifications of new food ingredients, food additives, etc. have been improved as following;
1) Revisions regarding fees for applications to approve or modify temporary standards and specifications for food products (under the Enforcement Rule of the Food
Sanitation Act) will be reflected in relevant forms, such as the approval application.
2) The scope of permissible modifications will be expanded, and a new processing timeframe will be established for food ingredients, allowing for changes to the target food products, usage amounts, manufacturing methods, and manufacturers, provided such as changes do not compromise safety.

G/SPS/N/CAN/1653.title: Proposal to modify two of the Lists of Permitted Food Additives (fruit and vegetable cellulose isolate); Proposal to modify the List of Permitted Food Enzymes (nuclease P1); and Proposal to modify the List of Permitted Food Enzymes (3-phytase)
G/SPS/N/CAN/1653.description:
Health Canada's Food and Nutrition Directorate completed premarket assessments of a number of food additive submissions seeking authorization for the use of: 

  • fruit and vegetable cellulose isolate as a stabilizing or thickening agent in cream for whipping at a maximum level of use of 2,000 ppm and as a bodying and texturizing agent or filler in various foods at maximum levels of use that vary according to the food;  
  • nuclease P1 from Penicillium citrinum NP 11-15 be authorized for use as a food enzyme in nucleotide-rich fish hydrolysate and nucleotide-rich yeast extract at a maximum level of “Good Manufacturing Practice” (GMP); and 
  • 3-phytase from Aspergillus niger NPH in plant-based products that resemble dairy products, as well as in plant-based products that resemble dairy-based products at a maximum level of “Good Manufacturing Practice” (GMP). 

 

The results of these premarket assessments support authorizing these additives for their requested uses. Consequently, Health Canada intends to enable the use of these food additives by modifying a number of the List of Permitted Food Additives, as described in this notice. 

The purpose of the information document is to publicly announce the Department's intention in this regard and to provide the appropriate contact information for those wishing to submit an inquiry or new scientific information relevant to the safety of this food additive.

G/SPS/N/CAN/1655.title: Modification to the List of Permitted Anticaking Agents (silicon dioxide)
G/SPS/N/CAN/1655.description:
Health Canada's Food Directorate completed a premarket assessment of a food additive submission seeking authorization for the use of silicon dioxide as an anticaking agent in nutrient pre-mixes for use in infant formula. 

 

The outcome of the premarket assessment supports authorizing silicon dioxide for use as an anticaking agent in nutrient pre-mixes for use in infant formula at a maximum level of use of Good Manufacturing Practice, with the silicon dioxide residue in the formula as consumed not to exceed 10 ppm. Consequently, Health Canada has extended the use of silicon dioxide as described in the Notice by modifying the List of Permitted Anticaking Agents, effective 29 October 2026. 

 

The purpose of the information document is to publicly announce the Department's decision in this regard and to provide the appropriate contact information for those wishing to submit an inquiry or new scientific information relevant to the safety of this food additive.

G/SPS/N/KOR/853.title: Partial Amendment Notice (Draft) of Standards and Specifications for Health Functional Foods (Advance Notice No. 2026-512, 23 October 2026)
G/SPS/N/KOR/853.description:
The proposed amendments seek to:

A. Reorganization of the structural framework of the Standards and Specifications for Health Functional Foods
(Draft Articles I.2, I.3, I.4, I.5, II.1, II.2, II.3, II.4, II.6, and [Annex 4])

  • The provisions for "Collection and Handling of Test Samples" were separated from the general standards and specifications, and "Raw Materials" was relocated to the general manufacturing standards, alongside the removal of unnecessary details and clarification of provisions.

B. Expansion of new ingredients for nutrients and establishment of specifications for ingredients to restructure the management system
(Draft Articles III.1.1, 4), 6), 7), and 8); III.1-1 4); III.1.1-4 4); III.1.1-11 1); III.1.1-16 1), 2), and 3); III.1.1-17 1), 2), and 3); and [Annex 5])

  • Three new ingredients, including calcium L-methylfolate, were added as manufacturing ingredients for folic acid, magnesium, and iron, and component specifications for magnesium and iron ingredients were newly established.

C. Improvement of the microbial specification application method for Ginseng and Red Ginseng concentrates
(Draft Articles III.2.2-1 2) and III.2.2-2 2))

  • The unit for the viable bacterial count specification for concentrates was changed from milliliter (mL) to gram (g).

D. Expansion of manufacturing methods for oils and fats containing EPA and DHA
(Draft Article III.2.2-16 1))

  • Additional manufacturing methods for EPA and DHA-containing oils and fats were permitted to broaden the scope of raw material supply and manufacturing options.

E. Further expansion of the recognized scope of raw materials for mucopolysaccharide protein
(Draft Article III.2.2-32 1) (1))

  • Reflecting scientific evidence secured after re-evaluation, "cartilage tissue of sturgeon and skate" was added to diversify raw materials and broaden manufacturing options, thereby strengthening the competitiveness of related products.

F. Expansion of the daily intake range for probiotics
(Draft Article III.2.2-51 3))

  • The upper limit of the daily intake for probiotics (10 billion CFU) was removed, changing the standard to "100 million CFU or more".

G. Clarification of daily intake for functional ingredients
(Draft Articles III.2.2-33 3), III.2.2-34 3), III.2.2-35 3), III.2.2-36 3), III.2.2-37 3), III.2.2-38 3), III.2.2-39 3), III.2.2-40 3), III.2.2-41 3), III.2.2-42 3), III.2.2-43 3), III.2.2-44 3), III.2.2-45 3), III.2.2-46 3), III.2.2-58 3), III.2.2-59 3), III.2.2-60 3), III.2.2-62 3), III.2.2-63 3), III.2.2-65 3), III.2.2-66 4), and III.2.2-68 3))

  • The daily intake of functional ingredients such as dietary fiber was modified to be based on functional (or marker) components.

G/SPS/N/KOR/854.title: Partial Amendment Notice (Draft) of Standards and Specifications for Health Functional Foods (Advance Notice No. 2026-513, 23 October 2026)
G/SPS/N/KOR/854.description:
The proposed amendments seek to:

A. Strengthening common manufacturing standards for functional ingredients (Draft Articles 2.1.3 and 2.2.3)
- Establish specifications for the use of mixed functional ingredients and other ingredients to prevent misuse and side effects and ensure safe intake by reflecting current consumption trends.
B. Revision of intake precautions for three types of functional ingredients (Draft Articles 3.2.2-6 3 & 4, 3.2.2-20 3, 3.2.2-54 3)
- Establish or amend precautions for green tea extract and shark liver oil containing alcoxyglycerol based on the review results of re-evaluations for the safety and functionality of functional ingredients.
- Amend intake precautions for theanine due to instances where it was inappropriately applied, not complying with its functional claim (e.g., “may help relieve tension caused by stress”).

G/SPS/N/MAR/123.title: Projet de décret modifiant et complétant le décret n° 2-10-473 du 6 septembre 2011 pris pour l'application de certaines dispositions de la loi n° 28-07 relative à la sécurité sanitaire des produits alimentaires
G/SPS/N/MAR/123.description:
Le présent projet de décret prévoit les amendements suivants :

  • la définition des termes « retrait » et « rappel » des produits ;
  • l’étalonnage et/ou la vérification des dispositifs de mesure ayant une incidence sur la sécurité sanitaire des produits alimentaires ;
  • la fixation d’une liste positive des arômes alimentaires et des auxiliaires technologiques autorisés dans les produits alimentaires ;
  • la suppression de l’obligation d’autorisation des prémélanges, des aliments composés et des aliments complémentaires pour animaux.

Les dispositions concernent également les équipements de mesure ou de surveillance utilisés dans les activités soumises aux exigences sanitaires et les procédures d'agrément des laboratoires privés

G/SPS/N/MAR/123.productsFreeTextPlain: Produits primaires et produits alimentaires destinés à la consommation humaine concernés par les nouvelles conditions de conformité, notamment en matière d'arômes alimentaires et d'auxiliaires technologiques ; aliments destinés à l'alimentation animale, notamment les prémélanges, aliments composés et aliments complémentaires. Les dispositions concernent également les équipements de mesure ou de surveillance utilisés dans les activités soumises aux exigences sanitaires et les procédures d'agrément des laboratoires privés

G/SPS/N/PHL/548.title: Implementation Guide on the Updated Regulations on the Importation of Dogs and Cats into the Philippines
G/SPS/N/PHL/548.description: This Circular is hereby issued to provide the updated  guidelines and implementation procedures for the importation of dogs and cats into the Philippines. It outlines the documentary and animal health requirements, including the approved Sanitary and Phytosanitary Import Clearance (SPSIC), rabies vaccination, parasite treatment, microchip identification, and among others. It must be noted that Philippines now requires Rabies Neutralizing Antibody Titer Test Result for each dog and cat entering the Philippines. Furthermore, Form 1 (Certificate of Animal Vaccination, Antibody Titer and Medication) is a mandatory document required during the application of SPSIC. This Circular also specifies the application process, required documents upon arrival, implementation schedule.

G/SPS/N/CAN/1651.title: Proposal to modify the List of Permitted Supplemental Ingredients (vitamin B6)
G/SPS/N/CAN/1651.description:
Health Canada initiated an evaluation to determine whether revised conditions of use for vitamin B6 in supplemented foods should be proposed based on the publication of an updated scientific opinion on the tolerable upper intake level (UL) for vitamin B6 by the European Food Safety Authority Panel on Nutrition, Novel Foods and Food Allergens (EFSA NDA Panel). Health Canada considered also considered control trials and case reports from the scientific literature, as well as information available in the Canada Vigilance Adverse Reaction Online Database.

The results of this evaluation support the revision of the conditions of use for vitamin B6 including the maximum permitted amounts in supplemented foods as well the threshold levels above which cautionary statements are required on the label.

Therefore, Health Canada proposes modifying the List of Permitted Supplemental Ingredients, as described in the information document cited above.

The purpose of this document is to publicly announce Health Canada’s intention in this regard and to provide the appropriate contact information for those wishing to submit comments, inquiries or new scientific information relevant to the safety of this food additive.

G/SPS/N/COL/441.title: Resolución 00021295 del 28 de octubre de 2026, "Por medio de la cual se suspende temporalmente la emisión de documentos zoosanitarios de importación (DZI) para aves vivas, productos y subproductos de riesgo susceptibles de transmitir la enfermedad de Newcastle, procedentes del estado de Santa Catarina, Brasil y se dictan otras disposiciones" (Resolution No. 00021295 of 28 October 2026 temporarily suspending the issuance of animal health import documents (DZI) for live birds, products and by-products at risk of transmitting Newcastle disease, coming from the state of Santa Catarina, Brazil, and issuing other provisions);
G/SPS/N/COL/441.description: The notified Resolution temporarily suspends the issuance of animal health import documents (DZI) for live birds, products and by-products at risk of transmitting Newcastle disease, coming from the state of Santa Catarina, Brazil. If live birds or products and by-products of avian origin arrive in the country, the consignment shall be reshipped or destroyed, as appropriate. Entry into the country is also prohibited for such products when covered by animal health import documents (DZI) issued by the Colombian Agricultural Institute (ICA) before the entry into force of the notified Resolution.

G/TBT/N/CHE/305.title: Draft Amendment of the Chemicals Act
G/TBT/N/CHE/305.description:
The national poison center provides important services to the public and healthcare professionals in cases of poisoning. However, the center’s funding is not adequately regulated. The current Chemicals Act provides for the designation and financial support of a poison center by the federal government. 
It should be amended so that chemical manufacturers are required to operate and finance a central poison center. A similar obligation should also be imposed on authorization holders for medicinal products and enshrined in the Therapeutic Products Act. The government should continue to provide financial support to the poison center.

G/TBT/N/CAN/784.title: Proposal to modify the Table of Chemical, Physical and the Nutritional Characteristics of Food
G/TBT/N/CAN/784.description:
Health Canada’s Food and Nutrition Directorate has launched a consultation regarding the notice of proposal to modify the Table of Chemical, Physical and Nutritional Characteristics of Food (Table).

The Food and Drug Regulations (FDR) include requirements related to protein quality that apply to the conditions for making protein content statements and claims and to the composition of foods in certain categories. The Table sets out the values (for example, protein ratings) and corresponding method(s) of analysis for demonstrating compliance with the these requirements. The “Digestible Indispensable Amino Acid Score” (DIAAS) method is not currently permitted to demonstrate compliance with these protein quality requirements. The “Protein Digestibility Corrected Amino Acid Score” (PDCAAS) method is permitted, however the prescribed methodology does not permit the use of protein digestibility values derived from in vitro assays (that is, non-human/animal). 

As described in the notice, Health Canada is proposing to authorize the use of the DIAAS method and two in vitro assays to determine protein digestibility values when using the PDCAAS method.

The modifications to the Table would come into force the day they are published on Health Canada’s website and would include:

  • the listing of the DIAAS method in the Table;
  • the incorporation by reference into the FDR (through the Table) of the document Determination of the protein rating using the Digestible Indispensable Amino Acid Score (DIAAS); and 

the modifications to the incorporated by reference document Determination of the protein rating using the Protein Digestibility Corrected Amino Acid Score (PDCAAS).
G/TBT/N/CAN/784.objectivesFreeText: The purpose of this communication is to publicly announce the Department's intention in this regard and to provide the appropriate contact information for those wishing to submit comments, inquiries or new scientific information relevant to this proposal.

The  Turkish Food  Codex  Communiqué on  Distilled Alcoholic Beverages  was notified to the WTO through G/TBT/N/TUR/71/Rev.1 on 31 July 2025. 

The Communiqué  has been published in the Official Gazette dated 1 October 2026, numbered 33387. 

Provisional Article

(1) Food business operators operating before the publication date of this Communiqué shall comply with the provisions of this Communiqué by 1 July 2027.

(2) Food business operators operating before the publication date of this Communiqué shall comply with the provisions of the Communiqué repealed by Article 22 until they achieve compliance with the provisions of this Communiqué.

(3) Products placed on the market before the publication date of this Communiqué or for which official import controls have been completed before that date may remain on the market for eighteen months from the publication date of this Communiqué.

G/TBT/N/TUR/200/Add.1.title: Turkish Food Codex Regulation on Food Additives
G/TBT/N/TUR/200/Add.1.description:
Turkish Food Codex Regulation on Food Additives was notified to WTO through G/TBT/N/TUR/200 on 23/06/2022.

The purpose of this Regulation is to modify the content of previously notified Regulation. The main amendments introduced in this draft are:

 

Following the entry into force of the Turkish Food Codex Regulation on Food Additives (Official Gazette Date: October 13, 2023, Official Gazette No. 32338, Supplement), which is harmonised with Regulation (EC) No 1333/2008, Türkiye has continued to align its legislation with subsequent EU amendments. Türkiye has also introduced a number of additional amendments considered necessary under national conditions.

 

•   The conditions for the use of E 476 polyglycerol polyricinoleate have been revised, permitting its use in “03. Edible ices and ice cream” and in emulsified sauces falling under food category 12.6.

•   E 267, buffered vinegar, has been added to the regulations as a new food additive. This food additive, which serves as a preservative and acidity regulator, has been included in Group I, and its use is permitted at the “quantum satis” level.

•   For E 249–250 nitrites and E 251–252 nitrates, the maximum permitted levels for addition in various categories, including meat, processed fish products, and dairy products, have been reduced. Furthermore, to more effectively monitor the total dietary intake of nitrites and nitrates, maximum limits have been established for residue levels from all sources throughout the shelf life of final products ready for market; the unit of expression has been changed from chemical formulas (sodium nitrite or sodium nitrate) to NO₂ and NO₃ ions.

•   E 483 Stearyl tartrate has been removed from the list of approved food additives. With this regulation, authorizations for its use as an emulsifier in all previously permitted categories, including flavored fermented dairy products, baked goods, and confectionery, have been revoked.

•    E 345(i) Trimagnesium dicitrate has been incorporated into the regulations as a new food additive for use in the “17.1 Solid dietary supplements” category. E 345(i) functions as a stabilizer and anti-caking agent in solid dietary supplements.

•  The name of category 14.2.8 has been changed to “Other alcoholic beverages, including other distilled alcohol-based beverages with an alcohol content by volume of less than 15%.” In addition, changes have been made to the permitted uses of certain food additives (such as specific groups of colorants and stabilizers) in some traditional fermented alcoholic beverages produced in the EU.

•   E 334 Tartaric acid (L(+)-), E 335 Sodium tartrates, E 336 Potassium tartrates, E 337 Sodium potassium tartrate, and E 354 Calcium tartrate have been removed from Group I and are now permitted only in specific categories with specified maximum usage levels. Their use in food enzymes and flavourings has also been restricted in Annex III.

•  In the “16. Desserts” food category, the scope of use for E 200–202 Sorbic acid — potassium sorbate has been expanded to include water-based gelatine-based desserts.

•   The scope of use for E 460 Cellulose powder and E 575 Glucono-delta-lactone has been expanded to permit their use in unripened soft spreadable cheese products within the “01.7.6 Cheese products” food category.

•   In the “04.1.1 Whole fresh fruits and vegetables” food category, the authorization for surface applications of E 471 mono- and diglycerides of fatty acids and E 903 carnauba wax for glazing purposes has been extended to include passion fruit, kiwi, and cassava. E 322 Lecithins and E 570 Fatty acids have been authorized under Annex III as carriers in preparations intended for polishing cassava.

•   E 960b Steviol glycosides produced by fermentation have been added to the regulations as a new food additive. This amendment includes E 960b in the existing “E 960a–960d: Steviol glycosides” group, allowing this sweetener to be used under the same conditions as other steviol glycosides.

•  In Annex III, Section 5, Part B, the authorization for the use of E 466 sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (cellulose gum) has been revoked.

•  In Annex III, Section 5, Part B, the use of E 301 sodium ascorbate has been authorized in microencapsulated vitamin A preparations used in infant and follow-on formulas.

•   In Annex III, Section 1, the scope of use for E 1202 polyvinylpyrrolidone has been expanded to permit its use as a carrier in colouring tablets intended for the decorative colouring of eggshells.

•   In the food category “16. Desserts; excluding products falling under categories 1, 3, and 4,” the use of E 200–202 sorbic acid—potassium sorbate is permitted only in unheated plant-based mousses.

•   The use of E 999 Quillaia extract is permitted in both solid and liquid food supplements (Categories 17.1 and 17.2). Additionally, provisions have been added to Annex III to allow its use as an emulsifier in flavourings.

•   E 412 guar gum has been banned in the “13.1.1 Infant formula” food category.

•  The following additions have been made to the list of food categories under Section D of Annex II:

         •    18.1 Processed foods not covered by Categories 18.2 and 18.3, excluding foods for infants     

         and young children

         •   18.2 Meal-replacement foods intended for weight loss

         •   18.3 Foods specifically manufactured to reduce the gluten content of gluten-containing 

         ingredients or to substitute gluten-containing ingredients

•    The following food categories listed under Annex II, SECTION D have been deleted. Authority over these categories lies with the Ministry of Health.

        •    13.1.4 Special medical-purpose dietary foods for infants and young children, as defined in     

        the Turkish Food Codex Regulation on Special Medical-Purpose Dietary Foods / Special   

        formulas for infants

        •   13.1.4.1 Dietary foods for special medical purposes for newborns and special formulas for 

        newborns

        •    3.1.4.2 Dietary foods for special medical purposes for infants and young children as defined 

        in the Turkish Food Codex Regulation on Dietary Foods for Special Medical Purposes

        •   13.2 Dietary foods for special medical purposes as defined in the Turkish Food Codex 

        Regulation on Dietary Foods for Special Medical Purposes (excluding those listed in category 

        (13.1.4))

•   E 942 The sale of nitrous oxide to the end consumer is prohibited.

•  The phrase “Non-alcoholic wine-like products” has been removed from the name of the food category “14.2.2 Turkish Food Codex – Wine Regulation: Wine and Other Products.”

•   In the subcategories under the “08. Meat” category, the definition has been used instead of the word “sausage.” The term “sausage” (sausages) is used in EU countries to refer to meat products served in casings and is not limited to the narrower meaning used in Türkiye.

•    To prevent the uncontrolled use of sorbic acid and benzoates, which may be present due to carry over from ingredients in meatless çiğ köfte products, under the category “12.7 Salads and savoury/spiced spreads for sandwiches,” the following limits have been established for meatless çiğ köfte: E 200–202 Sorbic acid — potassium sorbate; E 210-113 Benzoic acid—benzoates at a maximum usage level of 200 mg/kg for each additive group. 

•    In the “14.1.1 Turkish Food Codex Regulation on Fruit Juices and Similar Products,” pickle brine has been excluded from the list of foods in the “Fruit Juices and Vegetable Juices” category where Group I food additives may be used. The use of E 210–213 (benzoic acid—benzoates) is permitted at a maximum level of 200 mg/l.

•    Additional restrictions have been introduced in Annex VI, titled “Certain Products Produced in Türkiye and Food Additives Prohibited in These Products.”

        •    In sucuk: water-holding agents in the E 400–469 range, E 235 natamycin, and E 553b 

         talc are prohibited.

        •    In heat-treated sucuk, the following are prohibited: E 400–469, E 235 natamycin, E 243 

        ethyl laurol arginate, and E 553b talc.

        •    In pastırma, raw or cooked döner, poultry döner, and raw or cooked meatballs and poultry 

        meatballs, E 400–469 are prohibited.

        •    All additives are prohibited in ground meat kavurma.

•   In Annex VI, titled “Certain Products Produced in Our Country and Food Additives Prohibited in These Products,” certain food additives are exempt from these restrictions.

        •    While the use of all food additives is prohibited in çiğ köfte, meatless çiğ köfte, and mezze 

        (such as haydari, Arnavut liver, fava beans, shakshuka, hummus, and similar dishes), E 267 

        (buffered vinegar) is exempt from this prohibition.

        •    While the use of all food additives is prohibited in köme, pestil, bastık, walnut-stuffed 

        sucuk, and similar products, as well as in baklava, E 330 citric acid is exempt from this 

        prohibition.

 

This Regulation enters into force on the date of its publication with a transitional period as December 31, 2028. Products placed on the market before 31/12/2028 by food businesses operating before the publication date of the Regulation establishing this article, and foods containing these products, may remain on the market until the end of their shelf life.
